title: Delimitation Commission and Article 82/170 Dynamic
newsContext: Renewed debate on seat allocation between northern and southern states following proposed census resumption.
prelimsTraps: Can Delimitation Commission orders be questioned in court? (Barred under Article 329(a)).
Which amendment enacted the current seat freeze? (84th Amendment Act 2001, freezing seats until post-2026 census).
staticAnchors: Article 82 (Parliament readjustment) and Article 170 (State Legislative Assemblies composition).
Delimitation Commission Act orders carry force of law and cannot be reviewed by judicial scrutiny.
Federalism friction: Population control penalty vs democratic representation parity.

mainsSnippet.intro: Delimitation addresses the constitutional mandate of equal population representation per constituency.
mainsSnippet.wayForward: Institute bicameral rebalancing: expand Lok Sabha representation while giving equal state veto power in the Rajya Sabha.

title: SC on Right Against Climate Change & Great Indian Bustard
newsContext: Supreme Court (M.K. Ranjitsinh case) formalized the explicit right against adverse climate impacts while balancing overhead transmission line mitigation.
prelimsTraps: IUCN status of Great Indian Bustard? (Critically Endangered, Schedule I of WPA 1972).
Primary habitat? (Semi-arid grassland ecosystem; Thar Desert in Rajasthan & Kutch in Gujarat).
staticAnchors: Great Indian Bustard: Critically Endangered (IUCN Red List), Schedule I (WPA 1972), CITES Appendix I.
Constitutional synergy: Article 21 read with Article 48A and Article 51A(g).

mainsSnippet.intro: In M.K. Ranjitsinh (2024), the Supreme Court recognized the right to be free from climate change impacts under Article 21.
mainsSnippet.wayForward: Mandate underground lines in core habitats and standardize bird diverters in non-core corridors.

title: Gubernatorial Assent to State Bills: Article 200 Inaction
newsContext: State governments approaching the Supreme Court over inordinate gubernatorial delay in granting assent to state bills.
prelimsTraps: Does the Governor have absolute veto over ordinary bills? (No; if repassed by assembly, assent is mandatory).
Can money bills be returned for reconsideration? (No, under Article 200 money bills cannot be returned).
staticAnchors: Article 200 options: Assent, withhold, reserve for President (Article 201), or return 'as soon as possible'.
Shamsher Singh (1974) and Nabam Rebia (2016): Governor acts on aid and advice with narrow discretionary exceptions.
Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions recommend a 6-month disposal deadline.

mainsSnippet.intro: Article 200 outlines gubernatorial assent as a constitutional check rather than an obstructionist veto on elected assemblies.
mainsSnippet.wayForward: Establish formal constitutional conventions or procedural amendments prescribing a maximum 3 to 6-month window for bill disposal.

title: Remission Jurisprudence: Section 433A CrPC vs BNSS 473
newsContext: Judicial review of state executive remission orders granted without subjective satisfaction or presiding judge concurrence.
prelimsTraps: Can the Governor's pardoning power under Article 161 be restricted by Section 433A CrPC? (No; constitutional power overrides statutory limitations).
Minimum actual imprisonment mandated by Section 433A CrPC for life convicts with capital offenses? (14 years).
staticAnchors: Statutory limits: Section 433A CrPC (BNSS Sec 473) mandates a minimum 14 years actual imprisonment for offenses carrying capital punishment.
Bilkis Bano (2024) and Epuru Sudhakar: Executive remission remains subject to judicial review against arbitrariness.

mainsSnippet.intro: Executive remission reconciles retributive penal law with reformative justice, guided by objective statutory criteria.
mainsSnippet.wayForward: Institutionalize independent prison board reviews, mandate public justification for remission, and incorporate victim voice.

title: UN Plastics Treaty (INC) & Extended Producer Responsibility
newsContext: Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) deadlock over capping virgin plastic production versus focusing solely on downstream recycling.
prelimsTraps: Definition of microplastics? (Synthetic solid particles measuring less than 5mm).
Did the 2019 Basel Convention amendments regulate plastic waste? (Yes; placed hazardous plastic waste under prior consent procedures).
staticAnchors: Microplastics (< 5mm): Primary vs secondary; causes toxic biomagnification in marine food webs.
Plastic Waste Management Rules in India: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) targets and single-use plastic ban.
Global debate: Upstream cap on virgin plastic production vs downstream focus on circular recycling.

mainsSnippet.intro: The UN INC process aims to create the first legally binding multilateral environmental treaty targeting plastic lifecycle management.
mainsSnippet.wayForward: Adopt harmonized global polymer transparency metrics while providing green tech transition financing to developing economies.
